clean_repro.observed: HTTP 200 OK with insertCount=1, insertIds=[0]. API successfully accepted string-form vector instead of rejecting it.

violated_assumptions: Vector field should be array of floats ([[0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4]]), not string ("[0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4]")
API should validate data types according to schema (FLOAT_VECTOR requires numeric array, not string)
REST v2 API should reject type mismatches instead of silently coercing

contract_refs: constraint_id: milvus_type_float_vector_001 - FLOAT_VECTOR data type definition
constraint_id: milvus_type_float_vector_029 - Supported data type: FLOAT_VECTOR
endpoint: entities+insert - should validate field data types against schema
contract_grounding.note: Schema explicitly defines FLOAT_VECTOR as a vector data type (numeric array), not string. The contract expects strict type adherence.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST v2 insert → checkAndSetData (utils.go:466) → case FloatVector (utils.go:543) → json.Unmarshal dataString → type coercion
source_grounding.note: 源码接地发现: REST v2 的 checkAndSetData 函数在处理 FloatVector 时,先通过 fieldValue.String() 获取字符串,再用 json.Unmarshal 解析。当用户提供字符串形式的 vector ("[0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4]")时,第一次 JSON 解析将其识别为字符串,第二次 json.Unmarshal 又将其解析为数组,造成隐式类型强制转换。正确做法应该是检查 fieldValue.Type,如果是 gjson.String 则直接拒绝,要求数组格式。

cognition_match.developer_quote: REST v2 API fails to properly serialize/deserialize complex data types (shape_id: rest-v2-data-type-handling, symptoms: Returns wrong values for large integers, Array fields in raw protobuf format, AutoId not working for Int64 PK)
cognition_match.note: This defect matches the historical bug shape 'REST_v2_data_type_handling'. Milvus maintainers have acknowledged REST v2 API has systematic type handling issues (26 instances, confidence 0.95). This is another instance of the same pattern: accepting string where array is required.

contract.explicit_requirement: Vector field must be FLOAT_VECTOR type (numeric array), not string. Schema defines dataType as FLOAT_VECTOR, which is a vector data type requiring array format.
contract.source_evidence_if_suspect: Source code in utils.go:543-552 shows json.Unmarshal accepting both string and array formats without type discrimination, violating strict schema contract.

physical.objective_constraint: Vector data represents mathematical entities (points in high-dimensional space). These must be numeric arrays, not strings. String representation of arrays is a different data type with different semantics.

behavioral.graceful_mechanism: Dual JSON parsing - first parse outer JSON, second parse vector string as array. This 'graceful' handling is actually a type coercion bug, not intentional design.

perspective_analysis.aggregation_applied: verdict_A=CONFIRMED + verdict_B=CONFIRMED + verdict_C=CONFIRMED → final=CONFIRMED (all three perspectives agree this is a defect)

verdicts.rationale: Milvus REST v2 /entities/insert endpoint performs improper type coercion for FLOAT_VECTOR fields. When user provides vector as string ('"[0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4]"'), the API accepts it and converts to array, instead of rejecting it as type mismatch. This violates schema contract (FLOAT_VECTOR should be numeric array), creates type ambiguity, and matches historical REST v2 data handling bug pattern (26 instances). Source code (utils.go:543-552) shows dual JSON parsing without type checking, confirming this is a bug, not by-design behavior.
